minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted $100 fines on three non-compliant grease trap holders and approved two special town meeting transfers.
minutes.summary: Wright Pierce kicked off an update of the 2012 study on rerouting some Fitchburg sewage flow to Leominster, and the commission agreed to send flow data. The commission voted to apply the automatic non-compliance fine to three grease trap holders and approved transfers to special town meeting articles. The business manager reported on pump station maintenance, an inflow and infiltration sensor, and exterior upkeep. Election of officers was postponed for lack of a full board.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to apply the automatic non-compliance fine to three grease trap establishments that had not complied.
The commission voted to approve transfers to the FY24 special town meeting articles, drawn from two special funds.
Wright Pierce began updating the 2012 study of rerouting some Fitchburg sewage flow to Leominster; Paula will send flow data, including 2020 and 2021.
The commission agreed to resume random unannounced grease trap inspections, without a vote, and deferred the oil and water separator reporting form to the next meeting.
Election of officers was postponed because the full board was not present; the IMA discussion is set for open session on September 12.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates in Lunenburg depend on contracts with Leominster and Fitchburg, and the rerouting study and the Leominster rate renegotiation could change what the town pays for treatment.
Restaurants and other grease trap holders face fines and renewed unannounced inspections, and new oil and water separator permits are coming, so businesses may see new requirements and fees.
The special town meeting transfers draw on sewer special funds, so residents will be asked to vote on that spending at town meeting.
watch_next: September 12 meeting: the IMA discussion in open session, and the oil and water separator reporting form returning to the agenda.
Special town meeting on November 14, where the special fund transfers are on the warrant.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both votes, the two transfers, the main fees and contract amounts, and the Halloween cancellation. They differ on several details: the meaning of 'Leominster seven percent' and the '68' figure, the flow-data years, which towns Paula checks with on the separator form, and whether Reynolds was chair or acting chair. The main point is that our minutes apply the 7% to Leominster as well as Fitchburg, which the official minutes do not support; check the recording at about 556s.
